probe.format_note: 16:9 (736x414), 1420 frames, H.264; stereo AAC 44.1 kHz music bed (not analysed for tempo). Landscape reference: every composition must be re-laid for a 9:16 film (see risks).

rights_note: found by the owner on Pinterest with a style search (file «swiss design motion · 2.mp4»), given by the owner via Downloads/refrencee on 2026-11-03; origin not stated → plan mode ADAPT, never RECREATE
reference_name: گرادیان سبز با کارت و تایپوگرافی

mode.alt_film_mode: UI when the package launches an app, a tool, a service or a workflow (the reference is a design-studio promo: kinetic type lines, then glass UI cards and dashboards, then a closing question)
mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only (dark-green/lime glow gradients alternating with pale cream-green light beats, kinetic Swiss type with mixed light and extra-bold weights, a glowing accent object that leads every transition, design-tool selection boxes on key words, 3D gradient ribbon tubes, glass UI cards in perspective), never its shots one by one, its mark, copy, stock footage or UI contents (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL, and the reference is a short voice-style line-by-line reel ending on a question

ignored.why: all English copy ('Everything starts with a Spark', 'Idea', 'Sketch', 'Question', 'What if this could grow?', 'Turning Ideas into experiences', 'GROWTH', 'CLARITY', 'Not Clutter – Not Waiting', 'Just flow and simplicity', 'Design shapes the journey', 'Smart layouts', 'Clear actions', 'All crafted to move people forward', 'Because great design isn't just how it looks', 'It's how it works', 'Ready to grow?'); never reused as text, our words come only from the approved package

the eight-petal sparkle/flower mark that travels through the whole film is the reference's own signature mark; its shape is never copied — the role (one small glowing accent object that leads the eye and every transition) is reusable with an object taken from the voiceover or the brand's own mark
live stock footage of a person at a monitor (back of head, shallow depth of field); never reused; the beat may only use owner assets or a code-built scene
stock photo/footage of a smiling woman at a laptop inside the frame; never reused; the frame slot may hold only an owner asset or a code-drawn scene

third-party UI contents (dashboard 'Hi, Welcome back', charts with '100k', 'Hello, Lucy' weather card with '26 °C Rainy All', smart-home tiles with 45% / 60%, avatar, calendar 'July 2021'); never reused, our cards hold our own content and only sourced figures
the small line-drawn face doodles inside pale green bubbles are the reference's illustrations; never copied — only the idea of tiny hand-drawn accents popping around a hero element

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 of the full frame at 480 px, tile 4x3 (8 sheets, all viewed; frame time = (sheet-1)*6 + index*0.5 s); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found hard cuts at 14.2, 19.87, 23.8, 33.77 and 42.1 s (the change at about 10.45 s is a slit-wipe, not flagged); dense sheets fps=10 at 360 px of 1.9-3.1, 9.3-10.5, 13.7-14.9, 19.3-20.5, 23.4-24.6, 33.3-34.5 and 41.6-42.8 s (7 sheets, all viewed). Spans between those points come from the 0.5 s sheets, accurate to about ±0.25 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled. Music not analysed.

visual_language: A Swiss-style kinetic-type studio promo: about two thirds of the time is type, broken by geometric glow shapes, a glass UI dashboard, a tablet with a pop-out card, a curved tile wall and two image beats (live footage, a framed photo). Medium: 2D kinetic type and SVG geometry in code with 2.5D glass cards and a 3D-looking gradient ribbon tube. Typography: one geometric grotesk sans, small to medium size, mixing light and extra-bold weights inside the same line; the key word is extra-bold lime, sits in a design-tool selection box, on a gradient highlight block or in a pill; words resolve from a blocky glyph-scramble; some phrases enter wide letter-spaced and tighten; stacked lines with stepped indents. Rhythm: about 19 beats in 47 s (average about 2.5 s), only five hard cuts; most changes are continuous handoffs led by one small glowing accent object (it swallows a line, hops to the next word, swells and becomes a light slit that opens the next shot, becomes a vertical bar before a cut); words land every 0.25-0.3 s. Palette: two worlds — deep bottle green with teal and lime glows for the questions, and pale cream / mint / soft yellow for the answers — tied together by lime-yellow and dark green. Signature moments: the line swallowed by the accent icon; the neon ring that opens into overlapping circles; a word riding a rotating circle; the glowing slit wipe; the echo-stack word; the gradient ribbon that writes words and wraps an image over and under; the tilted glass dashboard assembling; the card popping out of a tablet; the light route drawn through a curved tile wall; the block-cursor statement stack.
look: Mostly 2.5D: flat type and thin geometric lines on soft blurred gradient grounds (large out-of-focus glow rings and blobs as the 'background feel'), with bloom/glow on every lime element (neon edges, light beams, glowing particles). Dimensional elements: frosted glass cards and panels with backdrop blur, thin bright rim and soft inner glow, tilted in perspective; a round gradient ribbon tube (dark green to lime) with soft drop shadow and over-under depth; glass tiles on a curved surface; a frosted glass circle with a thin dark outline on the light ground. No hard shadows; soft shadows only under the ribbon and floating cards. Motion blur on whips and the flying icon. Depth of field only in the footage beat. Two grounds: dark (deep green → teal glow) and light (cream → mint → pale yellow).
code_translation: Code-native. Type beats: DOM text in the brand fonts (light and extra-bold weights of the same family), split into words; each word enters as a scramble of solid bars (a few frames of blocky placeholder glyphs or a short horizontal stretch + blur) and resolves in about 0.15 s; staggered on the voice word timings; key word: extra-bold in the accent colour with an SVG selection box (thin rect + four corner squares drawn in about 0.2 s), a gradient highlight block wiping in behind it, or a pill sliding out; letter-spacing tighten-in (from about 0.5em to normal, 0.4 s ease-out) for Latin only. Accent object: one small glowing SVG shape (brand mark or a voiceover-driven icon) with a blur-layer bloom, animated along paths with squash and stretch, used for every handoff (swallow, hop, swell, slit wipe via an SVG mask that opens from a line). Geometry: SVG circles and rings with stroke-dashoffset draws and glow filters; a rotating group for the 'word on a circle'. Ribbon: SVG thick stroke with a linear gradient and a soft shadow, drawn by stroke-dashoffset, with over-under done by splitting the path into front and back layers around the framed image; text-on-path via SVG textPath (for Persian use whole words and check joining in the renderer, or set the words on a straight segment of the ribbon). Glass cards and tiles: DOM with backdrop-filter blur, rim gradient border, CSS 3D perspective for the tilted dashboard, the pop-out card and the curved tile wall (or three.js planes on a cylinder). Grounds: large blurred radial gradients and rings drifting slowly. Echo stack: cloned word layers with decreasing opacity collapsing to one. Motion blur by frame blending or directional blur on whips.
code_buildable_note: 47.35 s total; only r1-s7 (10.45-14.2 s, 3.75 s) is live footage of a person and is not buildable as shown (owner asset or a code-built scene instead); r1-s10's frame holds a stock photo of a person — counted as buildable because it is an image slot for an owner asset or a code-drawn scene; everything else is type, SVG geometry, glass UI and a gradient ribbon built in code.
continuity: One small glowing accent object travels through the whole film and leads every handoff: it swallows a finished line, hops to the next word, swells and stretches into a light line, and marks where the next scene begins.
A line of text collapses into the accent object (words squash and scramble back into bars), so the object carries the idea into the next shot.
A ring around the object opens into a larger geometric frame (overlapping thin circles), so the next scene grows out of the last element instead of cutting.
Slit wipe: the accent object stretches into a thin horizontal light line that opens like an eye onto the next scene.
Word morph: one word scrambles into the next in place (blocky glyph bars between the two), keeping the eye on the same spot.
Rotation carry: the camera rotates with a word riding a circle, and a fast whip along the curve becomes the next scene's blurred ring.
The ribbon thread: one gradient tube draws itself in one beat, exits, and re-enters the next beat to wrap the new subject over and under, carrying words along its path.
Collapse to a particle: a whole frame shrinks into a small square, spins into a tiny diamond and drops into the next dark scene, where cards then assemble around the space it left.
Pop-out: an element inside a screen lifts out into 3D space and becomes the subject of the next shot.
Light route: a glowing line draws a path through a grid and reveals the text behind its head, so motion and reading happen together.
Two grounds alternate as question and answer: dark green with glows for setups and questions, pale cream-mint for answers and payoffs; every switch is a hard cut on a phrase boundary.
Key-word marking is constant across scenes (extra-bold accent colour plus a selection box, gradient block or pill), so the viewer learns where the meaning sits.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its sparkle/flower mark, copy, stock footage and photos of people, UI contents (dashboard, weather card, smart-home tiles, figures), face doodles or the shot order one by one.

The reference is 16:9 (736x414) and the film defaults to 9:16: every composition (left-aligned lines, wide dashboards, curved tile walls, the image frame) must be re-laid vertically inside safe-zones.md; type is set larger than the reference's small lines (about 4% of a landscape frame height) to meet the minimum sizes.

Glyph-scramble, letter-by-letter typing, letter-spacing tighten-in, a single swapped letter and text-on-path all break or misjoin Persian letters: for Persian animate whole words only (blur/scale or a bar-mask reveal per word), accent whole words, keep tracking at 0, and put words on a straight ribbon segment or check joining before using textPath (rtl-grammar.md).

Directions read left → right (icon travelling right, pill sliding out to the right, slit opening from the left, card sliding off left, block cursor ahead of the word on the right, stepped indents to the right): for Persian they follow references/rtl-grammar.md.
Two beats depend on photos or footage of people (r1-s7, r1-s10): our film uses owner assets there or code-built scenes; never stock faces.

Lime-on-dark-green and dark-green-on-cream contrasts are fine for bold words but thin light-weight lime on the glow areas may fail contrast: readability ranks above the reference; check every line against the background under it.

Reference colours (deep bottle green, teal glow, lime-yellow accent, cream/mint light ground, orange-yellow icon) map onto brand colour roles (dark background, secondary glow, accent, light background, highlight); never used as literal hex values. Colours were read by eye, not sampled.
Heavy bloom, backdrop blur and CSS 3D on many cards are costly to render in headless Chromium; motion-build should cap the number of blurred layers per frame and pre-render glows where possible.
The reference has its own music bed; our cuts and reveals follow the voiceover first, and L6 sets sound. Tempo was not analysed.
The reference ends on a question with no logo: our outro follows the brand's own logo outro rules (router conflict order, item 5).
